name: nav-menu
description:
The full-screen menu a narrow `navbar` opens.

It was a centred column of large words on an INVERTED wash — the default full-screen menu that every site has, and nothing about it belonged to this brand. Rebuilt out of the devices the rest of the system already uses: an eyebrow naming the band, a left-aligned column with a real reading edge, a hairline rhythm between items, a marker bar on the current one, and a meta line saying what each destination IS. A menu of five words tells you their names; a menu with a line under each tells you which one you want.

LEFT-ALIGNED, and that is the biggest change. Centred display type is the generic answer, and it is also the harder one to read: five centred lines have five different starting points, so the eye re-finds the left edge on every row. Every other index in this system — the sidebar, the navbar, the footer — reads down a single edge, and this one now does too.

A SEPARATE composite from `navbar`, for a structural reason rather than tidiness. The bar is `backdrop-filter` glass, and a filtered element creates a containing block for `position: fixed` descendants — so a menu nested inside the bar is trapped in the bar's box and covers nothing. The real header found this and renders the menu as a SIBLING. Any implementation that nests this will look correct in a harness and fail on the page.

base.$description:
`position: fixed` over the whole viewport at the overlay layer — BELOW the bar, deliberately, so the bar's own control stays reachable and the menu cannot cover the thing that dismisses it.

A container like every other composite: `inset: 0` gives it a width from outside its contents, and the type below sizes in `cqi` so the menu is right at any size it is given rather than only at full screen.

IT DECLARES `--icon-tint`, the colour the engine paints a duotone's secondary layer with. Declared HERE, on the unit that draws the glyph, and not once at the document root: a global custom property is the anti-pattern the whole scoping design exists to avoid — two brands on one page write the same name and the second wins. An app shell is no better, because a shell is a container that may host more than one vibe. A unit is the smallest thing that owns its own subtree, so the tint travels with the component that needs it and reaches nothing else.

scrim.$description:
The ground, and it FOLLOWS THE THEME. It was `--color-primary` — marine in light, near-white in dark — so the menu was a dark takeover on a light page and a light one on a dark page, inverted against whatever the reader had chosen. That is the right call for `voice-pill`, which is chrome and has to read as the active layer; it is the wrong one here, because a full-screen menu IS the page for as long as it is open and a page that inverts when it opens is a page that changed.

97% rather than a heavy blur: frosted glass is the NAVBAR's device, and two glass layers in one interaction leaves neither reading as the front one. The page stays faintly present so dismissing feels like closing rather than navigating back.

close.$description: The close control's PLACE, sitting exactly where the bar's toggle sat. It wears `btn btn--neutral btn--shape-circle` — the same leaf, the same variant, the same shape as the hamburger it replaces — so the two are one control trading glyphs rather than two circles that happen to look alike. It carried its own border, radius, size and transition before, which is a button reimplemented in a menu.
close.insetInlineEnd: max(calc(var(--space-comfortable) - var(--space-tight)), calc((100% - var(--navbar-measure, 84rem)) / 2 + var(--space-comfortable) - var(--space-tight)))

panel.$description: The reading surface, and now also the frame the bar's chrome carries over into. The panel spans the NAVBAR'S measure (`--navbar-measure`, inherited from the header the island lives in) with the bar's own inline padding, so the crest opens exactly where the logo was and the close lands exactly where the hamburger was — the takeover reads as the same bar transformed, not as a different surface that happened to appear. The reading content (items, footer) keeps its own 46rem measure INSIDE that frame, because a menu row at 84rem is a line of text lost on a desktop.

head.$description: Mirrors `.navbar-bar` line for line: the same 3.5rem row height, the same vertical centring, the same tight gap the bar's brand cluster uses. The crest is the logo's 1.75rem box, in the logo's place.

crest.$description: The brand mark at the BAR'S size and place — 1.75rem, the `logo-mark` box. It was 36px floating in the panel's own padding, which put a second, differently-sized logo two hundred pixels from where the reader just saw the first one.

eyebrow.$description: Composes `text text--eyebrow`. The brand's signature device — it names the band the eye is about to read — in paradise, like every other eyebrow in the system. It was an inverted white at 70%, which was a second answer to a question the system had already settled.

items.$description:
A list with a rhythm, not a stack of words — each row carries a hairline above it, the same decision `sidebar` makes at a quarter of the size.

`safe center` and not `center`. Plain centring is right while the destinations fit and destroys the surface when they do not: the row refuses to shrink, the footer is pushed past the panel's bottom edge, and the language switch lands on top of the last item. The `safe` keyword centres while there is room and falls back to `start` the moment there is not, so nothing is ever centred into an overflow the user cannot scroll back to.

`min-block-size: 0` is what lets the row shrink at all — a grid child defaults to `auto` and will not go below its content, which is why `minmax(0, 1fr)` on the track was not enough on its own.

item.$description:
One destination. `clamp(1.75rem, 7cqi, 3rem)` in the display face — `cqi`, the container's inline size, not `vw`: the real header uses `11vw` and is right by coincidence, because there the menu happens to BE the viewport. Measured against its own container it is right everywhere.

The whole row is the target, and the row is padded rather than the text — a 3rem word with a 3rem hit area is a link you can miss above and below.
item.transition: background var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out), padding-inline-start var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out)

meta.$description: What the destination IS, under its name. A menu of five words tells you their names; a line under each tells you which one you want — and it is the difference between a splash screen and a table of contents.

marker.$description: The bar beside the current destination — the same device `sidebar` uses, at this surface's scale. Present on every row at `opacity: 0` and revealed by the selected state, so the current item settles rather than the bar appearing from nothing.

footer.$description: What sits under the destinations — the language switch, and a line saying who you are talking to. Separated by a rule rather than a gap: it is not the last item in the list, it is what the list sits above.

trust.$description: One quiet line. A page that ends on purpose rather than simply stopping — the composition rule this surface was missing.

social.$description: The social marks, in the menu. The bar hides its social row below 62rem — correctly, the bar has no room — but hiding them from the BAR must not hide them from the estate: on a phone this menu is the only navigation surface there is, so it carries what the collapsed bar sheds. Same `social-row` composite, left-aligned with the destinations.

tone.$description: The ground the menu lays over.

solid.$description: No blur — for a surface where the page behind is noise rather than context, and for the browsers that cannot do it.

hover.$description: The row tints and steps in. Moving the text rather than only colouring it is what makes a large target feel like a control — at display sizes a colour change alone is easy to miss, because the glyphs are mostly negative space.

selected.$description: The page you are already on: accent ink, and the marker bar revealed. `accent-ink` rather than the raw accent — sunflower at full strength on a pale ground is 1.7:1 and unreadable, which is the whole reason the ink role exists. Colour is never alone: the bar carries it too.

reducedMotion.$description: It still opens and every destination is still there; only the movement goes. Removing the ANIMATION without this would leave the panel at `opacity: 0` — the classic reduced-motion bug, where the transition was the only thing revealing the content.

a11y.note:
A visible CLOSE control, not only Escape — a full-screen takeover with no visible dismiss traps anyone who did not know the keyboard shortcut, and Escape is no help on a touch screen.

A dialog in everything but name: while it is open, focus is trapped inside it, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the toggle that opened it. The page behind is `inert` — without that a screen reader and a Tab key both walk straight through the scrim into a page the sighted user cannot see.

ONE navigation landmark, not two. The menu holds the same links the bar does, so it must be the same `<nav>` moved rather than a hidden second copy; two landmarks with one label is a screen reader announcing the navigation twice.

The current destination carries `aria-current="page"` and is marked by accent ink AND a bar, never by colour alone.

`visibility: hidden` rather than `display: none` in the closed state, so the open transition has something to animate from — and so the closed menu is genuinely out of the tab order, which `opacity: 0` alone does not do.
